newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends higher on Pakistan, spillover.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends higher on Pakistan, spillover.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended higher on support from news Pakistan bought 450,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat and on spillover strength from rallies in CBOT corn and soybeans, traders said.
Traders said KCBT May wheat gained relative to KCBT March as Rosenthal Collins, a commission house with large fund holdings, bear-spread four million May/March bushels at 30 to 32 cents per bushel.
The KCBT March/May spread, which climbed as high as 34 cents after the opening, narrowed to close on paper at just under 30 cents.

U.S. wheat markets surged early after Pakistan opted to buy 450,000 tonnes U.S. wheat. Pakistan had tendered for 450,000 tonnes Australian wheat as well but passed on that portion of the tender, Islamabad sources said.
CBOT corn futures surged on fund buying and on USDA cattle-on-feed data, and soybeans rallied on surprisingly high USDA weekly export inspections.
KCBT wheat settled 2-1/2 to seven cents per bushel higher, with March up 4-1/2 cents at $4.20.
Traders said commodity brokers E D & F Man International bought 2.2 million May bushels.
